question: How is the validity of the nonconceptual explained in the view that depends on conceptual construction?
premises: Some declare validity in dependence on conceptual construction.
That view still recognizes the nonconceptual.
The nonconceptual is reached through a sequence of concepts.
inference: Therefore, in that view, the nonconceptual has validity insofar as it is obtained through the ordered progression of conceptual constructions.
plain_english: Even in the view that makes validity depend on conceptual construction, the nonconceptual is still valid—but its validity is reached through the ordered sequence of those very concepts.
